newsitem.title: USA: Old crop US wheat at big discount in eastern belt.
newsitem.headline: Old crop US wheat at big discount in eastern belt.

text.p: The poor quality of what's left of the 1995-1996 soft red winter wheat crop in the eastern U.S. Midwest has forced some merchandisers to place unusually large discounts on any wheat graded below U.S. No. 2.
"We're heavily discounting anything under No. 2," said one Ohio-based merchandiser.
Some dealers in Indiana and Ohio will not accept any old crop wheat at all, and the discounts ranged from 45 to 70 cents per bushel for both SRW and white wheat, dealers said.
Typically, old crop wheat is not subject to such heavy discounts, merchandisers said.
The drastic discounts have discouraged some producers from bringing their wheat to market, dealers said.
"They're thinking that if they can hold off until February or March, we'll buy it, blend it and ship it out," said a merchandiser.

The old crop wheat is in poor condition because of the rocky 1995/96 growing season. Bitterly cold weather affected much of the crop when it was in dormancy. As a result, the crop was plagued by low test weights, broken kernels and some shrinkage, dealers said.

"It was a terrible year for growing," a Toledo-based merchandiser said. "We never got the snow cover in December, and when the plants came up in March, we saw a lot of green stuff that didn't mature."
Dealers said that much of the high-quality SRW old crop wheat had already been consumed, and it was a rarity to come across wheat graded U.S. No. 2 or above.
